additional_requirements: Functioning is not markedly impaired apart from the impact of the delusion(s) or its ramifications

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

symptom.disease_info: Delusional Disorder is characterized by one or more fixed delusional beliefs, typically lasting at least one month, with overall functioning often more preserved than in schizophrenia and without the broader psychotic symptom pattern of schizophrenia. The course is often chronic and circumscribed, with people commonly presenting only after the belief causes interpersonal, occupational, legal, or medical friction despite contradictory evidence.

patient.stressor: After Barrington led a successful countywide transportation safety initiative and received public recognition at a Sumter County meeting, he became unusually invested in the idea that the achievement had made him a target of people trying to discredit him. Over the next year, routine disagreements about inspection reports, budget questions about his vintage car spending, and harmless comments at car shows became incorporated into a fixed belief that others were working against him, even when supervisors and church friends calmly showed him evidence to the contrary. He continued working and stayed outwardly sociable, but the belief began to strain mentoring relationships and made routine compliance reviews tense. He came to psychiatric care after an employee assistance referral was framed as a way to help him manage the stress of an ongoing workplace conflict rather than as a challenge to his conviction.

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: I’m here because ever since that county safety award, certain people at work have been twisting my inspection reports and asking pointed budget questions like they’re trying to make me look crooked, and even when my supervisor says it’s just normal review, I can tell there’s a coordinated effort to discredit me.

add_requirements.Functioning is not markedly impaired apa: I still get to work on time, complete my inspections, keep up with church, and take care of myself; the main problems come up when people bring up those reports or question my spending.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: The biggest consequence is that compliance reviews and mentoring younger inspectors have gotten tense, and I’ve pulled back from a few coworkers I used to trust.
add_requirements.duration: This has been going on for about a year, ever since I got recognized for the county safety initiative.
